title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Says US Companies Should 'Absolutely' Use Chinese AI Models Despite Bessent's Sanctions Warning
key_facts: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang told Axios 'on Wednesday' that American companies should 'absolutely' use Chinese AI models, breaking from the hardline stance of Trump administration officials.
He said the concern should be the campaign to ban open-source models from China, and that there is 'no scenario where China runs U.S. companies off the road'.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had said on Tuesday that the US can sanction overseas model developers found stealing from American companies, and that the government sees watermarks of US-built language models on many AI models coming out of China.

Huang downplayed theft and distillation concerns, saying 'Distillation, learning from AI... is fundamental to intelligence', while adding that companies should be held accountable for breaking contracts or user privacy.

He opposed banning or restricting access to AI models in both the US and China and said Anthropic's Claude Mythos, a cyber-security model available to a limited set of US companies, 'should be available as a service'.
He argued that free, open AI is good for chips and data centres, and that the markets and Washington misunderstood the 'Kimi shock', as with DeepSeek's open model in January 2025.
The article gives no calendar date for the Wednesday and Tuesday; our 28 Sep 2026 edition carried this same Stocktwits article.
quote_evidence: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang on Wednesday broke away from Trump administration officials' increasingly hardline stance against Chinese AI models, saying that American companies should "absolutely" use them.
"If we see, especially, that overseas models are stealing from our great companies, we have the ability to sanction them because of this theft," he [Bessent] said on Tuesday.
"Free AI should be great for hardware. Free AI should be great for chips. Free AI should be great for data centers," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip maker's chief openly opposes a US sanctions threat against Chinese AI developers, but the interview is old.
event_date: A Wednesday before 28 Sep 2026 (not dated in the article)
